newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin sees government layoffs ending.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin sees government layoffs ending.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Tuesday that public sector layoffs would soon end and that the foundation for "very strong growth" had been laid.
"There is no doubt that the layoffs in the public sector at the three levels of government are obviously having an impact on job creation," Martin told reporters outside the House of Commons.
"However, we're beginning to see the end of that...and private sector job creation is increasing," Martin said.
Martin added: "Once the drag of the public sector layoffs is behind us, I think you'll obviously see a great deal of confidence coming back in the minds of consumers."
He was reacting to a Conference Board of Canada report on Tuesday that showed a marginal decline in consumer confidence.
"We have really laid the foundations for very strong economic growth. Our inflation is low. Our interest rates are low. Our productivity is up," Martin said.
He said business confidence has been higher than the historical average. That would translate into much more hiring in the future, which would renew consumer confidence.
